nodes.statement: The stdio MCP surface must stay byte-identical across releases; never change tool wire behavior without an explicit, separately-approved migration.
nodes.rationale: External consumers pin against exact stdio framing; a silent byte change breaks installed clients with no error. This is the frozen contract that makes the npm package safe to auto-update.
alternatives_rejected: let stdio output drift with refactors

nodes.statement: The anonymous remote MCP endpoint is frozen at exactly 45 tools; the golden sha256 of newline-joined sorted tool names is f64bb18529f458276acfe7886bd912165faa0b6f7d12025e51b79eb7782bb0a6.
nodes.rationale: The anon tool set is a published contract and a security boundary (no auth = curated subset). Any drift is a regression, caught by re-hashing tools/list from the live endpoint.
alternatives_rejected: let the anon set grow with each feature

nodes.statement: Production promotion to mcp.ravenmcp.ai is human-gated: Andrew only, a single supervised `vercel deploy --prod`, never `vercel promote`, never from web/.
nodes.rationale: The remote endpoint handles real user identities and per-user data; an unsupervised or wrong-project promote can expose or corrupt live state. The gate is a person, not a flag.
alternatives_rejected: deploy prod from the web/ project

nodes.statement: The canonical hosted MCP host is mcp.ravenmcp.ai, served by the `site` Vercel project (repo root), which also serves api/mcp.js, api/mcp-user.js, and OAuth well-known routes.
nodes.rationale: One canonical host avoids split-brain auth and well-known-route drift; `site` is git-integrated so it stays in sync, whereas web/ has no git integration.
alternatives_rejected: serve MCP from the web/ Next.js project

nodes.statement: Raven and Morven are separate products: all of Raven is in Morven, but not all of Morven is in Raven. Raven is the free open-source server for the solo indie dev, forever; Morven is the paid superset team platform.
nodes.rationale: Keeps the OSS free-tier promise credible while giving the paid team product room to hold hosted/creation/governance surfaces the OSS server should not carry.
alternatives_rejected: merge Raven and Morven into one paid product
put team/governance features in the free OSS server

nodes.statement: The hosted remote stack is WorkOS AuthKit for per-user OAuth plus Upstash Redis for per-user storage; free-beta access is via AuthKit only.
nodes.rationale: Per-user identity and isolated storage are required for the Taste Engine; WorkOS+Upstash is the committed, live-verified stack (delete/rate-limit/isolation proven).
alternatives_rejected: shared multi-tenant storage without per-user isolation

nodes.statement: The Next.js web/ project is the committed replacement for the static site/ marketing surface; web/ has no git integration and is deployed manually with `vercel deploy --prod` from web/.
nodes.rationale: Static site/ hit its ceiling; Next.js gives the marketing surface the polish the design-intelligence claim requires. The no-git-integration caveat is a known operational landmine, not a reason to revert.
alternatives_rejected: give web/ git integration on the same project as site

nodes.statement: PROPOSED (unresolved, awaiting Andrew): remove the silent install phone-home (scripts/postinstall.cjs POST to ravenmcp.ai/api/welcome) before cutting Raven 2.0, keeping the newsletter subscribe line. Not yet policy.
nodes.rationale: It is an undisclosed opt-out network call in an OSS package that returns the user nothing; for the cold indie-dev trust persona it is a launch-day liability. Install signal is better served by npm download counts plus the existing subscribe link, at zero trust cost.
alternatives_rejected: keep opt-out telemetry and disclose in README
flip to opt-in with no reciprocal user benefit (near-zero opt-in rate)
